_about: G1 고르바스의 발톱 — 카드별 장면 지시. 쓰는 법은 tools/art/PROMPT_GUIDE.md, 검사는 node tools/art/scene_tool.js lint G1.

CS-G1.scene: Centred and radial, seen from steeply above: one enormous bare footprint has just been stamped into red clay, and around it lie the remains of a trap made of pale cold light — a ring of half-risen jaws and snare loops, snapped in mid-spring, their bright fragments flying outward in every direction and dimming as they go. A second ring, of dust and clods, is still spreading from the heel. The toes of the print point toward the right.
CS-G1.light: Slate storm daylight; the dying trap fragments give the only cold glints, quickly swallowed by rust-red dust.

EP-G1-1.scene: Far below a towering mountain wall, small in the lower right of the frame, a one-eyed giant pit fighter stands with his back to us in a ring of trampled clay, one fist — sheathed in a gauntlet studded with black obsidian — raised over a fallen opponent's club. A wind-driven curtain of dust sweeps the crowd around the ring. High in the mountainside above, a slab of rock and pine forest has lifted like an eyelid, and one vast reptile eye looks down at him.
EP-G1-1.light: Sun through blowing dust; a broad pale shaft falls from the upper left across the open eye and down onto the ring.

EP-G1-2.scene: Side-on like a long frieze across the whole frame: three ranks of spearmen stand one behind another from right to left, and a woolly rhinoceros charging toward the left has already gone straight through the first two — each shows the same ragged gap, with spears and splintered shafts still spinning in the air above it. Its long forward horn is a hand's width from the third rank. A single war-painted rider lies flat along the shaggy ochre-brown hump, and rain and grit slant across everything.
EP-G1-2.light: A slate storm front fills the sky; one break of pale light travels with the rhino while the ranks stand in grey rain.

EP-G1-3.scene: Ground level on a windswept summit at night: in the snow of the foreground lies a trail of snapped spears, a cloven axe haft and a split war club, leading away up the slope. At the end of it, toward the left, a huge scarred silverback gorilla in hide fist-wraps stands hammering one fist against a curved grey claw as tall as a watchtower — the nearest of a row of claws rising out of the snow, each one a hill. A long sleeping breath from somewhere above flattens his fur and hurls ice dust past us.
EP-G1-3.light: Moonlight on snow, bone-white and grey-blue; the gale of breath carries glittering ice dust across the dark claws.

G1-01.scene: Straight overhead: a round duel ring of trampled clay fenced with crooked stakes, a single fire-bowl burning at its centre so that every stake throws a long shadow outward like a spoke. At the left edge a young bison calf — thin legs, a hump only beginning, horns still two short buds — has its forehooves inside the gate gap and its hind hooves still outside. Behind it runs a line of small hoofprints; ahead, clay churned by much larger hooves.
G1-01.light: Night; the fire-bowl is the only light, warming the clay ochre and stretching the calf's shadow back out through the gate.

G1-03.scene: First-person view from the foot of a rocky hill: a round pebble, huge and blurred, is already flying straight at us, filling the lower left of the frame. Up on a boulder at the right a big maned baboon holds the perfect follow-through of a thrower — long arm extended, weight on the front hand, dog-like muzzle split in a yellow-fanged grin. Beside its hind foot sits a tidy heap of chosen stones, sorted by size.
G1-03.light: Clear moonlit night; cold light from behind the hill rims the mane and the flying stone in bone white.

G1-04.scene: From deep inside an earthen den, looking out through its round mouth set left of centre: a hyena pup stands in the daylight outside, facing in, with a thigh bone as big as its own head clamped crosswise in its jaws — far too wide for the hole, jammed against both sides of the entrance. One round ear is freshly nicked, the spotted fur is dusty, and the eyes above the bone are bright with a giggle. Dark roots and packed earth fill the right of the frame.
G1-04.light: Sunlit dust haze glares outside the den mouth and spills a soft ochre wedge onto the tunnel floor.

G1-05.scene: Strict side view, flat as a frieze: three spotted hyenas pace in single file from left to right along the outside of a fence of rough stakes, high shoulders sloping to low hips, heads carried low. Between the stakes behind them only dust and the stamping legs of a crowd can be seen. The last hyena has its nose pushed between two stakes; the first has stopped in mid-step, one paw raised, round ears turned toward the noise.
G1-05.light: Slate storm light before rain, flat and shadowless, with red clay dust hanging at knee height.

G1-07.scene: From high above, looking down a long slope of dry grass: a dun-bodied centaur gallops toward the lower right of the frame, braided hair and mane streaming, and a single narrow wake of flattened grass runs back behind it all the way to the upper left corner — a whole day's run in one line. Its horn bow is at full draw for the first time, one obsidian-tipped arrow on the string, the quiver at its flank otherwise empty.
G1-07.light: Late-afternoon sun from the left lays long umber shadows across the straw-pale grass and lights the bow's horn edge.

G1-08.scene: Seen from behind, high on a cliff ledge in the upper half of the frame: a row of weathered grey boulders, and the middle one has shoulders. A hunter's spear, waterskin and bedroll have been propped against it for the night. Now two stone wings are lifting off its back, cracking a skin of lichen and spilling pebbles over the gear, and hooked stone talons flex on the ledge. Far below, past its folded haunches, lie the dark plain and a pale bend of river.
G1-08.light: A full moon from the upper left paints the granite bone-white; the land below is grey-blue dark.

G1-10.scene: Through a ragged hole torn in a windbreak of woven branches: beyond it a heavy boar, mud-caked, dark bristles up, stone-grey tusks low, is already twenty paces on and still running toward the right edge, small in the right of the opening. From the hole to its heels runs one straight, deep furrow of turned earth, clods still in the air, as neat as a ploughed row across the pale grass.
G1-10.light: Slate-grey storm light from a low sky; wind drives grit and torn grass sideways through the hole.

G1-11.scene: A mongoose spearman sits cross-legged just inside the triangular door of a hide tent, glimpsed from outside in the dark, lashing a jagged shard of black obsidian to its spear shaft. One end of the wet sinew is clamped in its small sharp teeth, the other wound tight by quick clawed fingers, and its long tail lies curled around its feet. The shard's broken edge catches the light like black glass, and chips of obsidian and two rejected points lie on a scrap of hide at its knees.
G1-11.light: One small tallow flame inside the tent lights its paws and jaw from below; the tent flaps are dark frames on both sides.

G1-12.scene: A stumpy young giant of cracked boulders, saplings and grass tufts sprouting from its shoulders, stands at the right and hurls a rock toward the left. Its throwing arm appears four times in one sweeping arc — cocked back, overhead, forward, flung open — each earlier arm fainter, like a trail of dust. The rock, the size of a cart, has just left the last hand. Behind the giant a hill stands unmoved, with two giant handprints pressed into its side.
G1-12.light: Slate-grey storm sky and flat cold light; grit streams off the arm at each of its four positions.

G1-13.scene: Dead-on and symmetrical: a rooster-headed beast sits low in the frame on a nest of twigs, stiff grey wings half spread, stone comb upright, both round eyes glaring straight at us while a scaly serpent tail coils around the eggs. Around the nest lies a perfect circle of grey gravel. At its rim things are caught in mid-change — a grass tuft whose near half is pebbles, a lizard of small stones, a dropped feather crumbling to grit.
G1-13.light: Hazy midday sun through dust, soft and shadowless, with ochre grassland glowing beyond the grey circle.

G1-14.scene: The whole frame tilts as a bull-headed giant charges straight at us, head down, eyes squeezed shut, iron nose ring swung flat by the speed. It has just burst through a stockade — split logs are still turning in the air behind it — and a splintered cart wheel and a length of fence rail hang impaled on its forward-swept horns from earlier collisions. One cloven hoof is about to land in the foreground.
G1-14.light: Hard afternoon sun from behind turns the churned dust into an ochre haze around the dark hide and horns.

G1-15.scene: From the ground among dry grass stems: a long, low lizard with black glassy scales and an ochre crest sprawls along the top of an obsidian outcrop in the upper frame, facing right, jaws clamped on the rock's edge as it grinds a claw against it. Flakes of black glass slide down toward us. In the blurred foreground stands a hare of grey stone, caught in mid-leap, with grass grown up around its legs.
G1-15.light: Low afternoon sun from the right; straw-pale grass glows around the black rock and each glass claw shows one hard white glint.

G1-18.scene: An enormous pot-bellied ogre kneels with its rump high and one cheek pressed flat to the ground, a black silhouette against a pale straw-coloured evening sky at the left of the frame. One hand is cupped behind a huge ear; the other is raised with a single finger up for silence. Bone charms hang from its neck as tiny dangling shapes. To the right the empty plain runs flat to the horizon, a few grass heads standing just as still.
G1-18.light: The sun has just set behind it; a low band of pale light outlines the whole shape and throws its long shadow toward us.

G1-19.scene: Over the shoulder of a war-painted rider sitting with arms crossed: ahead of us stretches the broad back of a cave bear, brown fur grown through with mossy stones like a hillside, the saddle strap lost among them. The bear lies flat with its chin on its paws and one eye half open, deciding. Beyond its ears, far down the pale slope, the dust of the rest of the war band is already moving away.
G1-19.light: Moonlight from high on the right silvers the stones on the bear's back; the plain below is grey-blue.

G1-21.scene: Tight on the upper body of a centaur at the left of the frame, in profile, aiming to the right: war-painted cheek pressed to the string, one narrowed eye, braided hair bound with bone beads. The horn bow fills the foreground, its stave cut with notch after notch from tip to grip, the newest still pale. The obsidian arrowhead points across the frame at a blurred distant line of fighters where one tall crested standard rises above the rest.
G1-21.light: Slate storm sky; a break of low light from the right picks out the notches and the black glass arrowhead, red dust in the air.

G1-23.scene: At eye level, a few steps away: a vast pot-bellied ogre walks toward us, filling the frame from edge to edge, a drum of stretched bear hide strapped across his belly and a thigh-bone beater in each fist. One beater has just landed — dust jumps off the drumskin in a ring, and the same shiver runs through his stomach, his bone charms and his heavy jowls. His small eyes are shut in concentration.
G1-23.light: A single campfire low on the left lights the drumhead and the underside of his arms warm ochre against the night.

G1-24.scene: A big scarred hyena stands laughing on a bare mound at the left of the frame, seen from low in the grass against the night sky. Its head is thrown back and to the left, high shoulders hunched, heavy jaws wide open. All along the bottom edge, round ears and pairs of eyes are rising out of the grass and turning toward it — the scattered pack arriving from every side.
G1-24.light: The dying embers of an abandoned cooking fire at the mound's foot light its chest and throat from below; stars behind.

G1-25.scene: A shallow rain pool on cracked clay fills almost the whole frame, and in it, upside down, stands the reflection of a hulking giant made of fractured boulders, turf and small pines on its shoulders, dull ochre light in the cracks of its face, one fist closing. The water answers the fist: tight rings of ripples cross the reflection and pebbles hop at the pool's rim. Along the top edge only its real stone feet are visible.
G1-25.light: Slate-grey storm sky mirrored in the pool, flat cold light, with ochre showing only inside the giant's cracks.

G1-26.scene: Extreme close-up of one eye of an old sabre-toothed cat, looking toward the right: heavy scarred brow smeared with rust-red war paint, tawny fur gone grey and stiff with dust, the curve of one long chipped fang rising into the lower corner. In the dark of the amber eye sits a small, sharp reflection — a saw-toothed mountain pass with a long column of followers pouring down through it, raising dust, the column wider at the near end than at the far.
G1-26.light: Hard sunlit haze from the right lights every scar and dust grain in the fur; the eye holds the brightest point.

G1-27.scene: Far across a thawing mountainside at night: patches of bone-white snow and bare ochre earth, and high on the right a small black cave mouth. In front of it a cave bear stands broadside, tiny at this distance, facing right, stones and moss humped on her back; two smaller shapes peer out from the dark behind her legs. A single line of footprints climbs the snow toward the cave, stops, and bends away in a wide careful arc.
G1-27.light: A high moon lights the snow patches bone-white and leaves the cave and the bear as dark shapes with pale rims.

G1-28.scene: Edge to edge, the frame is packed with running bison heading right — dark shaggy humps, short curved horns, rolling eyes, dust boiling up between the bodies so that only backs and heads surface, row behind row to the top of the picture. On one bull near the middle a snapped hitching post trails its rope and a dented cooking pot swings from a horn: whatever stood in the way is travelling with them now.
G1-28.light: Low sun from behind the herd turns the dust pale straw and edges every hump with light; long shadows fall toward us.

G1-29.scene: In pure profile on a bare ridge: a broad man-shaped figure of rough boulders stands facing left, each stone hanging a hand's width from the next, daylight showing through every seam and slow dust turning in the gaps where a deep ochre glow sits. The boulders are lichen-grey on their old faces and pale where they were freshly split. Behind its heels, at the right edge, a trail of smaller stones is still rolling uphill to join.
G1-29.light: Flat slate storm light from behind the ridge; the figure reads dark with ochre seams, grit blowing through the gaps.

G1-32.scene: From close behind, low to the ground: the thick tail of an ox-sized lizard lashes across the bottom of the frame, black glassy scales throwing off grit, and beyond it the broad armoured back races away toward the left horizon on splayed, clawed legs. On both sides the dry grass of the whole plain lies pressed flat in a single direction, baring streaks of rust-red clay, and a flock of startled birds lifts on the far right.
G1-32.light: Slate storm light from above, with one pale break at the horizon that slides along the wet-looking black scales.

G1-33.scene: Far up a long mountainside, small in the upper part of the frame, a giant of fractured boulders with a grove of pines on its shoulders stands frozen in mid-stride, climbing toward the right where a snow peak waits. Its footprints come up the slope from the lower left like a record of years: the nearest to us holds tall pines and the smoke of a small camp, the next young birches, the next only grass, and the newest, under its lifted heel, is bare red clay.
G1-33.light: Slate storm light over the whole slope, with a single pale shaft falling on the giant and its newest footprint.

G1-34.scene: A miner's shovel lies dropped on stony ground, and its worn-bright blade, filling the left half of the frame and tilted toward us, holds a reflection: a tall woman half turned to cracked grey stone, a crown of stone snakes rearing from her head, two eyes glowing dull ochre as she walks closer. Beside the shovel stand the boots and shins of its owner, already grey granite to the knee, with a fallen lantern still alight between them.
G1-34.light: The fallen lantern's small flame is the only light, warming the shovel blade and the stone shins from below.

G1-35.scene: The ground cut open in a clean cross-section: along the top runs a thin strip of sunlit grassland with a few tiny herd animals and a ring of standing stones, all tilting. Below it, through layers of clay, gravel and roots, a tunnel as wide as a canyon holds a colossal eyeless worm ringed with rock plates, its head in the lower right, round maw stretched wide in a yawn of stone teeth. Cracks climb from the yawn to the surface.
G1-35.light: Late sun lights the surface strip pale straw; the layers below darken from ochre to deep umber around the worm.

G1-36.scene: High behind his shoulders, looking down: a towering bull-headed chieftain stands at the left of the frame with his back to us, forward-swept horns spanning wider than a wagon, one hand resting on a stone-headed axe planted in the earth. He has simply stopped. Across the plain below him, thin dust trails from every direction are already bending toward the spot, and at his hooves tiny figures are stacking spears and digging the first fire pits.
G1-36.light: High hazy sun; the dust trails glow pale ochre against the darker grass and his shadow falls short at his hooves.

G1-41.scene: From underneath, looking up: the pale ribbed inside of a giant marsh-turtle shell fills the upper frame like a roof, held overhead by one thick grey-ochre arm. Beneath it the ogre's heavy-browed face looks down at us, patient, and pressed against his pot belly three small war-painted youngsters peer up from under the rim. Arrow shafts and slingstones clatter off the outside and drop past the edge of the shell.
G1-41.light: Grey storm daylight leaks in around the shell's rim; the faces beneath are lit softly by light bouncing off the pale ground.

G1-42.scene: Side-on, flat as a carving: a single dragon scale as tall as a hut stands upright on its edge in the right third of the frame, a curved slab of layered slate with turf and pebbles grown on its outer face, leaning slightly to the left as if bracing. On the ground before it lie dozens of snapped sword blades and split axe heads, and one sword still quivers where it has just struck. In the narrow lee behind it: undisturbed grass and a sleeping goat.
G1-42.light: Cold moonlight from the upper left whitens the slab's edge and the broken blades; ochre veins show faintly inside the scale.

G1-43.scene: From ground level behind it: a wall of huge boulders stretches across the whole frame, each stone hovering a finger above the earth, shoulder to shoulder, with dust curling in the seams and a dull ochre glow deep in the cracks; the middle stones form a rough head and two braced arms. Through the narrow gaps, the tips of halberds and the dust of an enemy line show on the far side. In the near foreground, bare heels step backward toward us.
G1-43.light: Sunlit dust haze from beyond the wall leaks through the seams in thin bright slits; this side lies in soft brown shade.

I2-2.scene: A rough double-bladed axe stands buried where its one blow landed, at the left of the frame: both crescent blades of dark chipped iron, lashed with rawhide to a haft as thick as a wrist, have gone clean through a tall enemy shield and on into the hard-packed earth beneath, splitting the shield from rim to boss. The haft still trembles, two wolf fangs swinging from it on a cord. In the grass behind lies the wielder's own small round shield, face down, thrown aside unscratched.
I2-2.light: Slate storm light from above; wind drives grit across the blades and into the fresh split of the shield.

IG1-1.scene: On a flat stone lies a hunter's hand strap, set right of centre — a band of dark rawhide cut to cross the back of a hand, with one long curved claw stitched to it in thick sinew, polished by wear, its tip chipped. Laid out next to it on the stone, in order, are the bleached toe bones of a great bear's paw: four still end in their claws, the fifth ends bare. A bone needle threaded with sinew rests between the two.
IG1-1.light: One small fire just out of frame on the left warms the rawhide and bone ochre and throws long soft shadows across the stone.

IG1-3.scene: A tattooist's work, half done: on a flat rock lie a row of bone needles lashed to short sticks, a small tapping mallet, and an upturned battered shield used as a tray for a mussel shell of dark red pigment. Stretched on a frame of sticks beside them is a patch of pale hide carrying the pattern — jagged interlocking fangs. The finished half of the pattern smoulders a dull blood red, as if lit from under the skin; the other half is still plain charcoal line.
IG1-3.light: Dim slate daylight under a storm sky falls from the left across rust-red clay; the red half of the pattern gives off a faint glow of its own.

IG1-4.scene: Set down at the left of the frame, far behind the fighting: a wooden back-frame with rawhide shoulder straps, and lashed into it a knee-high totem of grey rock — a heavy-browed face roughed out with a few deep cuts, banded with rust-red clay paint, a string of knucklebones around its neck. Its hollow eyes look toward the right, where a battle shows only as a thin line of dust on the horizon. The grass around the frame stands untrampled.
IG1-4.light: Late-afternoon sun from the right lays the frame's long umber shadow across pale straw grass and warms the painted bands.

IG1-6.scene: A chieftain's war axe rests across a rack made of two forked antlers, spanning the frame from edge to edge: a long haft of dark wood wrapped in braided hide and hung with a row of wolf fangs, and one broad bearded blade whose edge has been honed bright and whose back ends in a fang-shaped spike. Behind the rack two thick wooden posts stand one behind the other, and both have been cut through by the same slanting stroke — their upper halves lie together in the dust.
IG1-6.light: Hazy sun from the upper right; fine dust drifts through the light and the honed edge carries one pale line.

M2-1.scene: One broad tawny forepaw, cropped at the wrist, rests claws-forward at the right of the frame on a crumpled steel breastplate. Across the shaved skin above its four toes runs a fresh tattoo of interlocking fangs in soot-black line, the skin around it still raised and smeared with ash. The paw points toward the right; under it the breastplate is torn open in four parallel rips that match the claws exactly. A bone tattooing needle lies beside it on the metal.
M2-1.light: Cold moonlight from above gives the steel and the claws a bone-white edge; the tattoo lines stay deep black.

MC-01.scene: Straight overhead on a moonlit field of tall dry grass: across the left half of the frame a dozen wolves lie pressed flat in a wide crescent, each in its own dented hollow, grey backs level with the stems, ears folded, muzzles tucked so that every fang is hidden. Along the right edge the front of an advancing line has stopped short — a row of crested helms and levelled spears, the spear points wavering toward one hollow, then another.
MC-01.light: A high moon bleaches the grass bone-white and drops a small sharp shadow inside each wolf's hollow.

MG-01.scene: From the receiving side, the breath before it lands: a low row of hunched shoulders and grounded spear shafts crosses the bottom of the frame, dark and still. Above and behind them, out of the night, two great shapes are already in the air at the top of the picture, knees drawn up, and all that the light catches of them is the pale curve of bared tusks, the whites of eyes and the edges of two raised stone axes beginning to fall. Dust hangs where their feet left the ground.
MG-01.light: One small fire off to the left rakes the tusks and axe edges with warm ochre light; the rest is deep night.

MG-04.scene: Across a moonlit plain, small with distance, stands a row of low burial mounds, each marked with a weapon planted upright. From the top of every mound a thin stream of dust is rising and bending through the air toward one point high in the frame, where the streams knot together into a single enormous fist of packed earth and stone, knuckles down, hanging over the open ground beyond the last mound. The fist is one stream from finished, and already tilting to fall.
MG-04.light: Cold moonlight from the right whitens the mounds and the dust streams; the underside of the fist is dark ochre.

MG-05.scene: A slice through the earth, across the whole frame. On the surface at the far left, a row of heavy bare feet comes down together, seen only to the shin. Beneath them the layers of clay and gravel carry the blow to the right as a wave that grows as it travels — a faint ripple under the feet, a rolling swell in the middle, and at the far right a heave that splits the turf, where a line of boots staggers and spears tip against one another.
MG-05.light: Hazy sunlit dust above the surface; below it the earth layers show in bands of matte ochre and sandstone brown.

MG-13.scene: A great bleached skull of a horned steppe beast sits on a flat boulder in dry grass, caught halfway through a blow that comes from the right: its right half is still whole — smooth brow, one long horn, a dark eye socket — while its left half has already burst into chalk-white splinters and powder streaming away to the left. Between the two halves the air holds the faint shape of a huge fist made of dust. Buckled armour plates lie cast off in the grass below.
MG-13.light: Late-afternoon sun from the right; the flying bone dust glows pale straw and every splinter throws a long umber shadow.

MG-16.scene: From inside the collapse, falling with it and looking up: a ragged disc of slate-grey sky shrinks overhead, ringed by breaking edges of turf. Between us and the sky hang slabs of red clay, boulders, uprooted grass, spears, a cart wheel and small tumbling figures from both sides of the fight, all dropping together — one of them spread-eagled, another already twisting to land on its feet. Walls of raw red earth slide past on every side.
MG-16.light: Storm daylight pours down through the opening as the only light; red dust thickens it into a dim rust haze toward the bottom.

NG1-2.scene: Coming straight at us across the plain: a wall of sound made visible — a curved front of dust, torn grass and skipping pebbles as wide as the horizon, already bending back the long lances planted along the bottom of the frame and stripping the plumes from them. Behind the front, small on a long low ridge, an unbroken row of howling shapes stands with heads thrown back, crowded from one end of the ridge to the other.
NG1-2.light: Slate storm sky; the dust front is lit from above in dull grey-brown, darkest at its base where the grit flies thickest.

PI-G1.scene: Caught in mid-air above a trampled hilltop: a single huge gauntlet tumbles through the centre of the frame toward the left, flung away — layered ash-grey hide, knuckle plates of slate-dark scale, a cuff cut with row upon row of small notches, its wrist straps whipping behind it. The wind of its flight has pulled a spiral of dust up after it, and far below, small in the lower right, a crowd of onlookers has turned to follow it, every head tipped back.
PI-G1.light: A slate storm sky churns overhead; one break of pale light catches the knuckle plates and the trailing spiral of dust.

PN-G1-C1.scene: Looking down from the eye height of a grown fighter: a small sabre-toothed cub stands in the middle of the frame glaring up at us, chin out, a knucklebone tied in the tuft of its neck fur — and the two fangs it bares are as long and scarred as any adult's, far too big for its small jaw. Thick tawny legs and heavy paws of older brothers wall it in on both sides. Behind its heels a training post lies bitten clean in two.
PN-G1-C1.light: Grey storm daylight from above, even and cool, with pale grit settling on its shoulders and fangs.

PN-G1-C3.scene: Over the heavy shoulder of the camp's biggest fighter, whose war-painted neck and jaw edge the right foreground: he is looking up. In front of him, at the centre of a ring of hide tents, sits a lump of several dozen boulders fused into one rounded body with stubby limbs and a blunt head turned to the left, taller than the tallest tent pole, dust drifting from its seams. Children have already stacked a row of pebbles on its knee.
PN-G1-C3.light: One campfire at its feet lights the lower boulders warm ochre and lets the top of the hulk fade into the night.

PN-G1-E.scene: Straight down from the sky onto a steep mountainside: at the bottom of the frame a mammoth ploughs downhill through scree and old snow — domed, rock-crusted head, long spiralling tusks, a back of red-brown wool with one small war-painted rider clinging between the shoulders. Above it the whole upper frame is a spreading fan of landslide: tumbling boulders, red clay, uprooted pines and bursts of snow, its leading edge already at the mammoth's heels.
PN-G1-E.light: Slate storm light, shadowless; red clay dust and powdered snow boil up from the slide in pale clouds.

PN-G1-U2.scene: Square to the viewer and symmetrical, from the waist up, filling the frame: a hulking bear-man stands with arms hanging wide, human fingers ending in bear claws, rust-red war paint dragged through the fur of his muzzle and chest. Down the middle of his chest runs a row of old leather lacings from the day he tied the hide on — now sunk into living fur, the skin healed shut around every knot. A bone-charm necklace bites tight into his thick neck.
PN-G1-U2.light: Storm-grey daylight from directly above; grit blows across him from one side and the eyes sit in shadow under the brow.

PS-G1-1.scene: A rough stone rampart at the left of the frame is coming apart by itself, course by course: its top edge has already dropped into a ragged staircase, and loose stones are still hopping off each step and rolling into the grass, small puffs of dust marking where the last ones landed. Far off to the right, tiny in the battlefield haze, a handful of figures stand with heads thrown back and fists raised toward it.
PS-G1-1.light: Clearing sky after the fight; warm hazy sun from the right lights the settling dust and the pale faces of the stones.

RG1-1.scene: After it is over: an empty plain under a fading night sky, grass combed flat by the wind. Three tall crested helmets lie far apart in the dust, each beside a broken commander's standard, and around each one the ground is stamped with hundreds of paw prints and bare footprints running inward from every side like the rays of a star. A few tufts of grey fur and a dropped fang necklace are the only things still moving.
RG1-1.light: Last moonlight, grey-blue and cold, on bone-white helmets and standards, with the torn earth showing dry ochre.

RS-G1-1.scene: One steel breastplate, torn from its straps, turns in the air at the right of the frame and tells the whole attack: across its left side a crescent of deep fang punctures has buckled the metal inward, and straight through that weakened crescent runs a single long gash opened by an axe, bright at its edges. Snapped buckles trail behind it. Far beyond, small and already wheeling away through the grass, a great wolf carries a rider low on its back.
RS-G1-1.light: Low afternoon sun from the left flashes once on the gash and lays long umber shadows across the pale grass.

RS-G1-3.scene: At arm's length from the blow: the knuckles of a huge strap-bound fist, entering at the lower left corner, have just met bare ground, and from under them a crack is tearing away toward the upper right faster than the dust can follow — the two lips of earth already lifting apart like a split log, pebbles hanging in the air above the gap, the fissure forking as it races toward a dark palisade on the horizon.
RS-G1-3.light: A single torch lying in the dirt lights the knuckles and the near edges of the crack warm ochre; the far plain is black.

SG1-01.scene: Between two leaning boulders, from the end where the hunt is waiting, a narrowing gap frames a herd of steppe antelope squeezed into a stone funnel. The drive has sorted them: at the very front, alone in the gap and nearest to us, comes the thinnest one, limping, eyes wide, while the stronger animals are packed behind it shoulder to shoulder. Along the tops of the boulders run the pricked ears of wolves, keeping pace.
SG1-01.light: Grey storm daylight from behind the herd; grit hangs in the gap and the lead animal is rimmed in pale dust.

SG1-02.scene: Small with distance, on a slope of red clay, a beaten line is trying to leave the field: a dozen figures strung out across the frame, climbing toward the left, each one staggering, leaning on a spear or on a neighbour. Directly behind every one of them a single low grey shape has risen from the grass and matched its pace — one pursuer to each, close enough to touch. The lowest pair on the slope has already stopped.
SG1-02.light: Slate storm light, flat and cold, with rust-red dust smoking off the slope behind the climbing line.

SG1-04.scene: An emblem laid out in the dirt: at the right of the frame a dented enemy helmet sits on a short stake, and down the middle of its brow runs one thick thumb-drawn stripe of wet ochre clay, still dripping. At the foot of the stake stand a small clay paint pot and a tallow lamp. All around, just beyond the lamp's reach, pairs of eyes shine in the dark, every pair turned toward the stripe.
SG1-04.light: The single tallow flame lights the helmet and the wet stripe warm ochre and puts a point of light in each waiting eye.

SG1-09.scene: Extreme close-up of the line where two masses meet: from the right, a packed wall of shoulders in hide and bone armour has just slammed into a row of wooden shields on the left. Along the seam everything is breaking at once — bone plates on the right star with cracks and shed chips, while the shield boards on the left split along the grain, rivets springing out, a far deeper dent already folding the whole row backward. Ochre dust squirts from the seam like breath.
SG1-09.light: Hard hazy sun from above; the flying chips and the dust in the seam hang bright against the dark crush of bodies.

TK-G1-1.scene: First person, looking down the length of our own long shadow stretched across pale dry ground: out of the shadow's chest a spotted hyena is climbing as if out of a pool — head, bristling shoulders and forepaws already solid and leaping at us with jaws wide, hips and hind legs still flat black shadow lying on the earth. A few grass stems lean away from it.
TK-G1-1.light: Low late sun from behind us makes the shadow long and sharp and lights the hyena's face full on.

TK-G1-2.scene: A black outline against a column of firelit smoke: a heavy-shouldered hyena stands on a lip of rock in the upper part of the frame, facing left, high withers sloping to low hips, stiff mane along the spine, head lowered with the jaws hanging open on a low laugh. One scarred ear is cut clean against the light. Loose dust still slides from its flanks as if it had stepped out of the ground a moment ago; the hollow below it is dark.
TK-G1-2.light: A single watchfire hidden in the hollow lights the smoke behind it warm ochre; everything in front is night.

TK-U-WOLF.scene: At eye level, as if standing a few steps away: a lean ash-grey hyena trots off toward the right edge of the frame with a single long bone carried crosswise in its jaws, glancing back at us over one high shoulder with a round ear cocked. Its paws leave a neat line of prints in the dust, the hindmost already thinning into drifting grit. Behind it on the left, a trampled patch of ground and one abandoned boot are all that remains of the fight.
TK-U-WOLF.light: Slate-grey sky after a storm; soft even light, red clay dust settling low over the ground.

UN-G1.scene: Seen from behind, at the height of his shoulders: the great chieftain stands in the right third of the frame on a rise of bare rock, a massive sabre-toothed cat with a ruff of bone-tied braids, one forepaw planted on a beaten enemy's crushed war horn, head thrown back in a roar, long fangs black against the light. Across the wide plain before him five long plumes of dust race in from the horizon and converge on him like the strokes of a claw — hyenas at full run, the nearest already close enough to count their spots.
UN-G1.light: A low sun straight ahead of him backlights the five dust plumes pale straw and cuts his figure almost to silhouette, rim-lit along braids, shoulders and fangs.

UN-G1-7.scene: One charge shown as five overlapping moments across the whole frame, right to left: the same broad mandrill, scarlet-and-blue ridged muzzle and golden beard, appears five times, each figure more solid than the last. At the far right he swings a plain bone club; next he holds a foe's short sword; then a long brass-bound halberd; then a gilded mace; and at the far left, fully solid, he straightens up with an elegant curved blade just lifted from an open hand on the ground. Behind each figure the weapon he dropped is still falling.
UN-G1-7.light: A full moon behind the last figure throws the row into hard light and deep shadow, each stolen weapon catching one bright edge.

UP-G1-11.scene: The frame tilts with its lunge: the same mongoose spearman drives forward and down toward the left, hind leg stretched, long tail streaming, both clawed paws sliding along a sinew-bound shaft. The spearhead leading the picture is a long, clean leaf of knapped black obsidian. On a cord around its neck three older points — chipped, snapped, worn short — swing out with the motion, and red dust sprays from its planted front foot.
UP-G1-11.light: Storm light from the right skims the obsidian edge and the three old points; the sky behind is slate, the ground rust red.

UP-G1-18.scene: From behind his broad, hide-draped back at the left of the frame: the enormous pot-bellied ogre sits cross-legged before a drum made of hide pegged over a pit in the ground, one huge ear still tilted downward, one palm just fallen on the skin. Ahead of him the plain itself replies — the earth has risen into slow concentric ridges like rings on a pond, grass riding their crests, pebbles hanging a hand's width in the air, the farthest ring reaching the hills.
UP-G1-18.light: Slate storm sky over the plain; flat grey light with brown grit lifting off each ridge of earth.

UP-G1-24.scene: Tight on the head and humped shoulders of a huge old hyena, filling the frame and turned toward the right: one ear torn to a stump, three sets of healed claw scars across the broad muzzle, bristling mane, heavy jaws just parting for a laugh. Behind it, soft with distance, the whole plain is holding still — a hundred hyenas sitting upright in the grass, a herd of antelope with every head raised, a flight of birds hanging as if pinned to the air.
UP-G1-24.light: Windless late afternoon; low sun from the left rakes the scars and mane and leaves the still grass pale straw.

US-G1-1.scene: Seen from the side across a storm-dark plain: a heavy throwing blade spins from left to right high over two facing battle lines, its flight drawn as a long arc of scattered dust, and the grass beneath that arc is parting into a straight open lane as both lines pull back from it. The blade is a heartbeat from landing point-down at the feet of the tallest figure on the right — a towering armoured champion who has already lowered his visor toward it.
US-G1-1.light: Slate storm clouds split along the same arc, and one hard shaft of light follows the blade down onto red clay.

US-G1-2.scene: From just behind a line of stamping heels at the bottom edge, looking out along the blow: the plain ahead has stopped being flat — a long hump is travelling away from us under the grass like a shrug under a blanket, lifting boulders and whole stands of pine, and at the horizon it breaks the surface as a ridge of slate-grey scales the size of hills. An enemy line caught on its slope is sliding off both sides.
US-G1-2.light: Low sun from the left throws the travelling hump's long umber shadow across pale straw grass; dust lifts off the scales in bright veils.

IR-G1.scene: Straight down onto a tattooist's hide mat beside a small fire. In the left third a palm-wide swatch of pale cured hide is pegged flat, and on it the tattoo's pattern stands finished in ash-grey ink: a mane of long swept strokes, each tapering to a point as fine as a blade tip, all the points meeting at one small dot. Laid out around it are a bone tapping comb with stained teeth, a worn striker rod, a horn cup of grey ash paste and a twist of coarse grey hair tied with sinew.
IR-G1.light: A single small flame just past the right edge warms hide, horn and bone in dry ochre while the rock around the mat sinks into deep darkness.

NG1-1.scene: The aftermath on a hillside camp: at the right, under a hide lean-to, three stretchers lie empty with their lashings burst outward, and unwound bandages, a snapped crutch and a splint trail out of the shade in a line. From there a swathe of gouged footprints plunges straight down the slope, each print deeper and wider than the last, to a rolling wall of rust-red dust far below — and inside the dust run small dark figures, every one with two points of red where the eyes would be.
NG1-1.light: High dry sun in a tan dust haze; the lean-to throws one hard shadow, and the red cloud below stands matte against the pale clay slope.

PN-G1-R.scene: Tight on the head and shoulders of a rangy ram at the centre of the frame, turned to the right: heavy curled horns chipped along their ridges, a scarred muzzle, rust-red paint across the brow, fleece rubbed grey with ash. He lowers his horns in challenge, eyes fixed on someone beyond the right edge, and a thong strung with dozens of stone chips hangs at his throat. At both edges the cropped shoulders of two companions lean in, lowering their own horned heads the same way. Behind them a long streak of grey smoke lies along the night horizon.
PN-G1-R.light: A high moon from the left edges horns, brow and ash-grey fleece in bone white, with grey-blue night behind and dry ochre earth under the smoke.

PS-G1-2.scene: Shadows on a canyon wall tell it. At the bottom a single small fire burns on the canyon floor, and around it sit the dark backs of a wolf pack of every size — a heavy leader with its head thrown back in a howl, lean yearlings, a cub half their height. On the sandstone wall that fills the centre of the picture every one of their shadows has risen to the same towering size as the leader's: a row of identical huge wolf-shapes with lifted muzzles, climbing toward the rim of the rock.
PS-G1-2.light: One small fire at the foot of the wall is the only light, warming the sandstone in dry ochre and leaving the canyon above in deep darkness.

RS-G1-2.scene: A round hide shield has just hit the dust, face up, at the bottom of the frame, a ring of grit still jumping from under its rim. The rust-red clay handprint stamped on it is lifting off the hide as one bright thread and streaming away from us along the ground to the next shield in the file, upright a pace behind, where a second handprint is appearing over the first. Beyond that, shield after shield recedes into the sunlit haze, each stamped with a single red hand, with only dusty boots showing beneath.
RS-G1-2.light: Hard midday sun through tan dust lights the file from the left; the red thread and the handprints are the only saturated colour in the clay-brown haze.

SG1-03.scene: Flat on our back on cold ground, looking straight up: from every edge of the frame bone-white stone fangs as long as spears close in toward the centre, the inside of one vast bite coming down on us, with the full moon caught in the shrinking gap between their points. Torn loose and tumbling up into that gap are a sword, highest and smallest, then a wrenched-off shoulder plate, then a helmet only just lifted away, its straps still flying, while grit sifts down from the fangs onto us.
SG1-03.light: A full moon directly overhead backlights the ring of fangs, bone-white on their inner edges and grey-blue in shadow, with dry ochre grit drifting through the beam.

SG1-08.scene: The ground has grown teeth. Across the whole frame rust-red clay is splitting open, and up through every crack push bone-white fangs — hundreds, from thumb-sized to tall as fence posts, thickest at the left — each pair snapping shut on whatever struck there: a sword blade bent double, a spear shaft bitten through, an empty iron-shod boot, an axe head. Chips of steel and clods of clay hang in the air above the bristling field, and at the far right the last heels of a charge are turning to run.
SG1-08.light: Slate-grey storm light from above flattens the red clay, and each fang shows chalk-pale against it while ochre dust blows through the gaps.

SP-G1.scene: The whole frame tips as the plain lurches. At its centre, veiled in dust and seen from a far ridge level with his shoulders, a mesa-tall titan of cracked sandstone and granite kneels and sets the knuckles of a hide-strapped boulder fist against the earth like a knock on a door. Cracks race outward from the fist through a ring of standing stones that reach only to its lowest knuckle, and hide tents the size of pebbles slide askew below us. From his bowed head and shoulders a mane of grey ash pours away across the sky.
SP-G1.light: Midday sun strained through tan dust falls in pale shafts across his sandstone shoulders, and the ash mane lays a long grey shadow over the plain.

SR-G1.scene: A hilltop shrine in tall dry grass: at the centre a broken fang of weathered bone stands point-up, tall as a great pine, its snapped root sunk in the earth, and the steppe has taken it back — turf has swelled around its base like a gum, lichen maps its sunward side, grass seeds in every crack and a crust of dry clay climbs it in rings. Sun-bleached hide cords circle its girth, a ladder of lashed poles leans a third of the way up, and offering bowls the size of thimbles dot the turf below.
SR-G1.light: Late afternoon sun from the left warms the bone's sunward side to dry ochre and lays its long umber shadow across the straw-pale grass.
